questions.question: A fruit seller had some apples. He sold 40% apples and still had 540 apples. The number of apples he had originally was:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Apples left after selling 40% apples = 540 apples

**Concept:**

A percentage is a number or ratio expressed as a fraction of 100.

To calculate the per cent of a number, divide the number by the whole and multiply by 100. Hence the percentage means, a part per hundred.

**Calculation:**

According to the question

Total apples = 100%

Remaining apples = 100% - 40% = 60%

So, 60% apples = 540 

⇒ 100% apples = (540/60) × 100

⇒ 900 apples

**∴ The fruit seller originally had 900 apples.**

questions.question: The monthly salaries of an officer and a clerk are in the ratio 11 : 4. If the monthly salary of the officer increases by ₹7,000 and that of the clerk by ₹3,000, then the ratio becomes 19 : 7. What was the initial salary (in ₹) of the officer?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The ratio of the salary of an officer and a clerk = 11 : 4

The monthly increase in officer's salary = Rs.7000

The monthly increase in clerk's salary = Rs.3000

The ratio of their final salaries = 19 : 7

**Calculation:**

Let the monthly salary of an officer = 11x and that of a clerk = 4x

Increased salary of the officer = 11x + 7000

Increased salary of the clerk = 4x + 3000

The ratio of final salaries = 19 : 7 

∴ (11x + 7000)/(4x + 3000) = 19/7

⇒ 7 × (11x + 7000) = 19 × (4x + 3000)

⇒ 77x + 49000 = 76x + 57000

⇒ x = 57000 - 49000

⇒ x = 8000

Initial salary of the officer = 11 × 8000 = Rs.88000

**∴ The initial salary of the officer was Rs.88,000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5058e5fd55e234f44849e5ba40bb29aebcd2d87bb65e80b310e42d057a222393.png] 

Using ratio method

⇒ (11 × 7) - (19 × 4) → (19 × Rs.3000) - (7 × Rs.7000)

⇒ 77 - 76 → Rs.57000 - Rs.49000

⇒ 1 → Rs.8000

⇒ 11 → 11 × Rs.8000 = Rs.88000 

∴ Initial salary of the officer = Rs.88,000.

questions.question: A 253 m long train running at a speed of 60 km/h takes 42 seconds to cross a bridge. The length (in m) of the bridge is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Length of train = 253 m

Speed = 60 km/h

Time = 42 seconds

**Concept used:**

Distance = Speed × Time

The distance covered by the train in crossing the bridge will be equal to the sum of the lengths of the train and the bridge.

**Calculation:**

Distance covered by the train = length of train + length of bridge

Speed = 60km/h = 60 × 5/18 m/sec

⇒ 50/3 m/sec

Distance covered = speed × time

⇒ 50/3 × 42 = 700 m 

∴ Length of bridge + Length of train = 700

⇒ Length of bridge + 253 = 700

⇒ 700 - 253 = 447 m 

**∴ The length of the bridge is 447 m. **

questions.question: By selling a guitar for ₹846, Rima loses 6%. For how much should Rima sell it to gain 8%?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Selling price = Rs.846

loss % = 6%

**Formula used:**

Gain = SP - CP

Gain % = Gain/CP × 100

Loss = CP - SP

Loss % = Loss/CP × 100

Where CP = Cost price, and SP = Selling price

**Calculation:**

Let the CP be 100a

Loss = 100a × 6/100 = 6a (∵ loss is 6% of CP)

SP = CP - loss

⇒ 100a - 6a = 94a

According to the question, 

94a = Rs.846

1a = Rs.9

100a = Rs.900 

CP = Rs.900

Gain = 8%

Gain = 900 × 8/100 = Rs.72 (∵ gain is 8% of CP)

SP = CP + Gain = 900 + 72 = Rs.972

**∴ To gain 8% Rima should sell it for Rs.972**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Loss = 6%

Then according to the formula

⇒ 6 = {(CP - 846)/CP} × 100

⇒ 6/100 = 1 - 846/CP

⇒ 846/CP = 1 - 0.06 = 0.94

⇒ CP = 846/0.94

⇒ CP = Rs.900

Now, Gain = 8%

⇒ 8 = (SP - 900)/900 × 100

⇒ 0.08 = SP/900 - 1

⇒ SP/900 = 1.08

⇒ SP = 1.08 × 900 = Rs.972

∴ To gain 8% Rima should sell it for Rs.972

questions.question: Excluding stoppages, the speed of a bus is 60 km/h and including stoppages, it is 42 km/h. For how many minute does the bus stop per hour?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Direct formula for stoppage time per hour:

Stoppage time = [(Faster Speed − Slower Speed) ÷ Faster Speed] × 60 minutes

Stoppage time = [(60 − 42) ÷ 60] × 60

Stoppage time = (18 ÷ 60) × 60 = 18 minutes

**∴ The correct answer is 18 minutes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f40ffa92fe01c310ae1df00b8e279247a7b54615d0fddb7ae77b2052b4831398.png] 

**Given:**

Speed without stoppages = 60 km/h

Speed with stoppages = 42 km/h

**Formula Used:**

Stoppage time per hour = Distance not covered due to stoppages ÷ Speed without stoppages

**Calculations:**

⇒ Distance covered in 1 hour without stoppage = 60 km

⇒ Distance actually covered in 1 hour with stoppage = 42 km

⇒ Loss in distance due to stoppage = 60 − 42 = 18 km

⇒ Time required to cover this 18 km at the normal speed of 60 km/h represents the total stoppage time.

⇒ Time = Distance ÷ Speed

⇒ Stoppage time = 18 ÷ 60 hours

⇒ To convert into minutes, multiply by 60.

⇒ Stoppage time = (18 ÷ 60) × 60 = 18 minutes

**∴ The correct answer is 18 minutes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average Speed with Stoppages

It is the total distance traveled divided by the total time taken, including both driving time and the time the vehicle was stationary.

Average Speed without Stoppages

It is the total distance traveled divided by the actual driving time only, completely ignoring any stopping periods.

Direct Formula for Stoppage Time

Stoppage time per hour = (Faster speed − Slower speed) ÷ Faster speed. To get the time in minutes, simply multiply the fraction by 60.

questions.question: What is the compound interest (in ₹, nearest to a ₹) on a sum of ₹8,000 for 21 over 8 years at the rate of 16% p.a., interest compounded yearly?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Principal = Rs.8000

Time = 21 over 8 years

Rate = 16% p.a.

**Formula used:**

Amount = Principal × (1 + Rate/100)ⁿ

Where n = time

The effective rate percentage for two years at R% p.a. = R + R + R²/100

Where R% is given rate per cent per annum

**Calculation:**

The effective rate of interest for the first two years at the rate of 16% p.a.

⇒ 16 + 16 + (16 × 16)/100 = 32 + 2.56

⇒ 34.56%

For the remaining 1/8 year, Rate = 16/8 = 2% p.a.

 ∴ The effective rate of interest for the total time period of 21 over 8 years

⇒ 34.56 + 2 + (34.56 × 2)/100

⇒ 36.56 + 0.6912

⇒ Effective rate % = 37.2512%

Compound Interest = 8000 × 37.2512/100

⇒ 80 × 37.2512

⇒ 2980.09

**∴ The compound interest is Rs.2980.**

questions.question: Find the compound interest, if ₹3,000 was invested for 3 years at 20% p.a., interest compounded half yearly (nearest to a rupee).
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Principal = Rs.3000

Time = 3 years

Rate = 20% p.a. compounded half yearly

**Formula used:**

Amount = Principal × (1 + Rate/100)ⁿ

where n = time

Effective rate of interest for 2 years = R + R + R²/100

Effective rate of interest for 3 years = 3R + 3R²/100 + R³/10000

Where R = rate of interest per annum

**Calculation:**

Since it is compounded half-yearly, the rate of interest is considered for the half year

∴ Rate = 20%/2 = 10%

Time = 3 years, which is equal to 6 half years

∴ n = 6

Now, for compound interest

Amount = Principal × (1 + Rate/100)⁶

⇒ 3000 × (1 + 10/100)⁶

⇒ 3000 × (11/10)⁶ 

⇒ 3000 × (1.1)⁶ = 3000 × (1.21)³

⇒ 3000 × 1.771 = 5314.683

⇒ Amount = Rs.5314.683

Interest = Amount - Principal 

⇒ 5314.683 - 3000

⇒ Rs.2314.683 ≈ Rs.2315

**∴ The Compounded interest compounded half yearly is Rs.2315**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__** Effective rate of interest for 3 years

⇒ (3 × 10) + {3 × (10)²}/100 + 10³/10000

⇒ 30 + 3 + 0.1

⇒33.1%

The effective rate for 6 years = 33.1 + 33.1 + (33.1)²/100

⇒ 66.2 + 10.9561 = 77.156%

compound interest = Principal × effective rate of interest for 3 years

⇒ 3000 × 77.156/100

⇒ 2314.68 ≈ 2315

∴ The Compounded interest compounded half yearly is Rs.2315.

questions.question: A man spends 74% of his income. If his expenditure increases by 30% and savings increase by 25%, then by what percentage will his income increase?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Expenditure = 74% of the income

Expenditure increases by 30%

Savings increase by 25%

**Formula used:**

Income = Expenditure + Savings

Percentage increase = {(New value - Old value)/Old value} × 100

**Calculation:**

Let the income be 100

Expenditure = 100 × 74/100 = 74

Savings = 100 - 74 = 26

Now, Expenditure increases by 30% and savings increases by 25%

New Expenditure = 74 + 74 × 30/100 = 74 + 22.2 = 96.2

New savings = 26 + 26 × 25/100 = 26 + 6.5 = 32.5

New income = 96.2 + 32.5 = 128.7

Percentage increase in income = {(New income - Old income)/Old income} × 100

⇒ {(128.7 - 100 )/100} × 100 

⇒ 28.7%

**∴ The percentage increase in income is 28.7%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__** Using the weighted average method

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ec29fcdeac96994c0b536d69dc42754b759de0a78d1f568e6bf33eca12cb0c62.png] 

Percentage increase in Income = 25% + (5% × 37)/(37 + 13)

⇒ 25% + 185%/50 = 25% + 3.7%

⇒ 28.7% 

∴ The percentage increase in income is 28.7%.

questions.question: One-third of the goods are sold at 15% profit, 25% of the goods are sold at 20% profit, and the rest of the goods are sold at 10% loss. If a profit of ₹350 is earned in the entire transaction, then the original value of the goods (in ₹) is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let the total value of goods be 1200 units (LCM of 3 and 4).

Profit on 1/3rd (400 units) at 15% = +60 units; Profit on 1/4th (300 units) at 20% = +60 units.

Loss on remaining goods (500 units) at 10% = −50 units.

Net profit = 60 + 60 − 50 = 70 units = ₹350 ⇒ 1 unit = ₹5.

Total original value = 1200 units × 5 = ₹6000.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹6000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Fraction of goods at 15% profit = 1/3

Fraction of goods at 20% profit = 25% = 1/4

Remaining goods = 1 − (1/3 + 1/4) = 1 − 7/12 = 5/12 (sold at 10% loss)

Total profit earned = ₹350

questions.question: The distance between two stations A and B is 700km. A train covers the journey from A to B at a speed of 80 km/h and returns back to A with a uniform speed of 65 km/h. The average speed of train during the whole journey, is closes to:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Distance between A and B = 700 km

Speed of train from A to B = 80 km/h

Speed of train from B to A = 65 km/h

**Concept used:**

Distance = Speed × Time

Average speed = Total distance travelled/Total time taken

**Calculation:**

Time taken by train from A to B = Distance/Speed = 700/80 

Time taken by train from B to A = 700/65 

Average speed during the whole journey = Total distance/Total time

⇒ (700 + 700)/[(700/80 + 700/65)]

⇒ (700 + 700)/[700 × (1/80 + 1/65)]

⇒ (2 × 700)/[700 × (13 + 16)/1040]

⇒ 2/(29/1040)

⇒ (1040 × 2)/29 = 71.72 km/h

**∴ The average speed of the train during the whole journey is 71.72 km/h.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] **__Shortcut Trick__** 

If the distance travelled in both the cases is same, then we can apply this formula,

Average speed = (2 × product of the two speeds)/(Sum of the two speeds)

⇒ (2 × 80 × 65)/(80 + 65)

⇒ 10400/145 = 71.72 km/h

∴ The average speed of the train during the whole journey is 71.72 km/h.

questions.question: A single discount equivalent to three successive discounts i.e. 7%, 12% and 5% is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Three successive discounts are 7%, 12%, and 5%

**Concept used:**

Discount = original value × (1 - R%)

Where R% = rate of discount percent

If R₁ and R₂ are two rates of discounts, then

Successive rate of discount = R₁ + R₂ - R₁R₂/100

**Calculation:**

Let the original value be 100

Applying discounts

⇒ Discounted value = 100 × (100 - 7)/100 × (100 - 12)/100 × (100 - 5)/100

⇒ (93 × 88 × 95)/10000

⇒ 77.748

Equivalent discount = (100 - 77.748)/100 × 100 = 22.252% 

∴ A single Equivalent discount of three successive discounts of 7%, 12% and 5% is 22.252%.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**If X% and Y% are two different rate of discounts. Then,

Effective Rate of discount = X + Y - XY/100

Effective discount rate of 7% and 12% will be

⇒ 7 + 12 - (7 × 12)/100

⇒ 19 - 0.84 = 18.16%

Now, the effective discount rate of 18.16% and 5%

⇒ 18.16 + 5 - (18.16 × 5)/100

⇒ 23.16 - 0.908 = 22.252 %

**∴ A single Equivalent discount of three successive discounts of 7%, 12% and 5% is 22.252%.**

questions.question: In a sale, perfumes are available at discount of 25% on the selling price. If a perfume costs ₹6,873 in the sale, what is the original selling price of the perfume?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Discount% = 25%

Selling Price = Rs.6873

**Formula used:**

Discount = Marked Price - Selling Price

Discount percentage = (Discount/Marked price) × 100

**Calculation:**

Let the original selling price or marked price be Rs.x

Discount = x - 6873

Discount % = 25 = {(x - 6873)/x} × 100

⇒ 25/100 = 1 - 6873/x

⇒ 1/4 = 1 - 6873/x

⇒ 6873/x = 1 - 1/4

⇒ 6873/x = 3/4

⇒ x = (6873 × 4)/3

⇒ x = Rs.9164

∴ The original selling price of the perfume is Rs.9164.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__** Let the original selling price or marked price be 100

Then, Discount = 100 × 25/100 = 25

Selling price = 100 - 25 = 75

But, according to the question, the selling price after discount is Rs.6873

∴ 75 = Rs.6873

⇒ 1 = 6873/75

⇒ 100 = 100 × 6873/75 = Rs. 9164

∴ Original selling price = Rs.9164.

questions.question: One year ago, the ratio of the ages of A and B was 4 : 3. The ratio of their ages, after 7 years from now, will be 9 : 7. What is the present age (in years) of B?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The ratio of ages of A and B one year ago = 4 : 3

After 7 years from now, the ratio of their ages = 9 : 7

**Calculation:**

Let the age of A, one year ago = 4x and 

Age of B one year ago = 3x

Then, Present age of A = 4x + 1

And present age of B = 3x + 1

After 7 years,

A's age = 4x + 8

B's age = 3x + 8

The ratio of their ages after 7 years = 9 : 7

⇒ (4x + 8)/(3x + 8) = 9/7

⇒ 7 × (4x + 8) = 9 × (3x + 8)

⇒ 28x + 56 = 27x + 72

⇒ x = 72 - 56 = 16

⇒ 1/Total time = (3 + 2)/30 

⇒ 1/Total time = 5/30 

⇒ 1/Total time = 1/6

⇒ Total time = 6 days

**∴ 15 boys and 12 girls work together and complete the work in 6 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e28cc3eb434f17ca093117e3c009312321d7b72bbbe9cffc8696bcc8944b6067.png] 

Efficiency of 15 boys = 3 units/day

Efficiency of 12 girls = 2 units/day

Total work = 30 units

Time taken by boys and girls together to complete the work = 30/(3 + 2)

⇒ 30/5 = 6 days

∴ 15 boys and 12 girls work together and complete the work in 6 days.

questions.question: A certain sum amounts to ₹12,740 in 4 years and to ₹15,925 in {7{1 over 2}} years at the same rate percentage per annum at simple interest. The sum (in ₹) and the rate percentage per annum, respectively are:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The first amount = Rs.12740 in 4 years

The second amount = Rs.15925 in {7{1 over 2}} years

The rate is the same for both amounts and is calculated at simple interest.

**Formula used:**

Simple interest = (P × R × T)/100

Amount = P × (1 + RT/100)

Where P = principal, R = Rate of interest, T = time 

**Calculation:**

Let the Rate of interest be R % and the Principal be P

Then, according to the formula 

⇒ 12740 = P × (1 + (4R)/100) ---(1)

also, 15925 = P × (1 + 15R/200) ---(2)

On dividing both the equations, we get

12740/15925 = 2 × (100 + 4R)/(200 + 15R)

⇒ 4/5 = 2 × (100 + 4R)/(200 + 15R)

⇒ (100 + 4R)/(200 + 15R) = 2/5

⇒ 5 × (100 + 4R) = 2 × (200 + 15R)

⇒ 500 + 20R = 400 + 30R

⇒ 10R = 100 

⇒ R = 10%

Now, from equation (1)

12740 = P × (1 + 40/100)

⇒ P = 12740 × 100/140

⇒ P = Rs.9100

**∴ Principal = Rs.9100 and Rate percentage per annum = 10%.**
